title: ArcCivs miner speed, resident supplies and corpse retention
assumptions: Baseline miner work is read from ArcCivs HEAD c67edf6: 4 seconds per native work action, doubled to 8 seconds at hunger <= 6. The 2-second healthy and 4-second hungry durations are implemented in the candidate CivsWorksites.kt; runtime throughput remains unmeasured.

Low/base/high scenarios use 1/10/16 participating cities, one quarry miner per city and 0.25/1/4 active work hours per city-day. These are sensitivity assumptions, not measured participation or worker-hours.

The ideal healthy excavation ceiling is 900/1800 one-block actions per active hour before/after; the hungry ceiling is 450/900 actions per active hour. These ceilings exclude travel, support placement, native work budget, night, failures, downtime, tool availability, storage and all other bottlenecks; they are not expected or measured throughput.

For the item scenario only, each counted excavation is assumed to remove plain STONE and yield exactly 1 COBBLESTONE. Actual native drops depend on the block and held tool; the scenario does not claim every mine cell is plain stone or has this drop.

A working adult loses 1 hunger per active minute and consumes 1 existing BREAD at hunger <= 14, restoring 6 hunger. The model uses the sustained upper bound of 10 bread per active worker-hour, or 2.5/10/40 bread per city-day at 0.25/1/4 hours; the initial food reserve and interruptions can lower actual use.

Hall supply is modeled as a transfer of up to 4 existing BREAD per refill, not an item grant. One/three/ten refill events per worker-day are upper-bound activity assumptions for 0.25/1/4 active hours; actual transferred amounts may be lower and unused bread remains inventory.

The current economy inventory's illustrative death scenarios of 0/0.1/1 resident deaths per city-day are reused only as sensitivity assumptions, not telemetry. The illustrative loadout is 16 BREAD, 4 profession tools and 4 armor pieces, not the native bag capacity limit. After death, the candidate behavior places those exact existing items in a lootable corpse for five minutes; unclaimed corpses expire. Escrow totals show temporary access opportunity, not guaranteed player recovery, new items or sustained net-supply change. No claim rate is assumed.

Builder paid sessions change from 8 to 64 already-paid rows. The existing serial placer remains capped at 4 placement units per second; accepted row costs and material requirements do not change, and no extra construction items or refunds are modeled. If the current MAX_POPULATION * BUILDER_SESSION_ROWS work-credit formula remains, the stored-credit cap scales from 96 to 768; this is backlog capacity, not placement throughput.

Vault and premium-token direct flows remain zero. Internal profession points are not player XP. No item-to-money rate is inferred; current EconomyShopGUI SELL and the planned future SELL-to-contract change are outside this assessment.

flows.basis: One miner per city; 0.25/1/4 active hours per city-day; 4s to 2s per action gives 225/900/3600 to 450/1800/7200 one-block actions per city-day. Assumes 1 COBBLESTONE from each plain STONE cell solely for this scenario; no terrain/drop distribution is measured.

Existing-item consumption at the sustained upper bound: 1 hunger/minute, 1 bread consumed at <=14 and +6 hunger, yielding 10 bread per active worker-hour. Assumes 0.25/1/4 active hours per city-day; same food rule before and after.

Illustrative loadout of 16 existing bread per death using the inventory row's explicit 0/0.1/1 deaths-per-city-day sensitivity; not measured contents or death frequency. The candidate corpse leaves this item available for up to five minutes, but actual recovery is unknown.

flows.source: ArcCivs candidate five-minute resident corpse inventory
flows.basis: Temporary escrow of up to 16 existing bread per death under the same illustrative 0/0.1/1 deaths-per-city-day assumptions. It is lootable for five minutes and expires if unclaimed; no item is issued and the number actually recovered is unknown.

Up to 4 existing bread per refill moved from hall storage into a resident's bag; 1/3/10 refill events per city-day are upper-bound assumptions corresponding to 0.25/1/4 active hours. Gross inventory movement only, not a grant; actual stacks can be smaller.

Illustrative loadout of 4 existing profession tools per death; 0/0.1/1 deaths per city-day are reused illustrative assumptions, not telemetry. The candidate corpse temporarily retains the exact existing tools; actual recovery is unknown.

flows.source: ArcCivs candidate five-minute resident corpse inventory
flows.basis: Temporary escrow of up to 4 existing profession tools per death under the illustrative 0/0.1/1 deaths-per-city-day assumptions. Five-minute lootability and expiry do not create items; actual recovery is unknown.
